title: Shin or sin, and the five final letters
topic: שׁ (sh) and שׂ (s); the five final letters ך ם ן ף ץ
why: The last letter of the alef-bet: the sin (שׂ), which differs from the shin only by its dot. You also review the five final forms and the order of the 22 letters, along with everyday wishes (birthdays, holidays).

{"lessons": ["

Shin or sin?

LetterNameSound
שׁshinsh (dot at the top right)
שׂsins (dot at the top left)

It's the same letter; only the dot changes. A trick: dot on the right (יָמִין, yamin, right) = sh; dot on the left (שְׂמֹאל, smol, left) = s. And שְׂמֹאל itself starts with a sin!

שָׁלוֹם — שָׂמֵחַshalom: hello — same'akh: happy
שֶׁמֶשׁ — עֶשֶׂרshemesh: sun — eser: ten

Without vowels (on the street, in the newspaper), nothing tells shin and sin apart: you recognize the word. And in שָׂמֵחַ, as in פָּתוּחַ, the a under the final ח is read before it: sa-me-akh.

", "

The five final letters

Five letters change their shape at the end of a word. Don't panic: the sound doesn't change.

LetterNameSound
ךfinal khafkh: מֶלֶךְ
םfinal memm: שָׁלוֹם
ןfinal nunn: גַּן
ףfinal fef: כֶּסֶף
ץfinal tsadits: עֵץ

Four of them go down below the line (ך, ן, ף, ץ); ם, on the other hand, is a closed square.

The normal form comes back as soon as the letter is no longer at the end: מֶלֶךְ but מַלְכָּה (malka, queen).

", "

The whole alef-bet

Here are the 22 letters in order. The word alef-bet comes from the names of the first two: אָלֶף, בֵּית.

א ב ג ד ה ו ז ח ט י כ ל מ נ ס ע פ צ ק ר ש תalef, bet, gimel, dalet, he, vav, zayin, khet, tet, yod, kaf, lamed, mem, nun, samekh, ayin, pe, tsadi, kuf, resh, shin, tav

With the sin, you can wish people all sorts of things:

יוֹם הֻלֶּדֶת שָׂמֵחַ!Happy birthday! [yom huledet same'akh!]
חַג שָׂמֵחַ!Happy holiday! [khag same'akh!]
שָׁנָה טוֹבָה!Happy New Year! (at the Jewish New Year, in the fall) [shana tova!]

שָׂמֵחַ agrees: a man says אֲנִי שָׂמֵחַ, a woman אֲנִי שְׂמֵחָה (smekha).
